contract_plain_english: In the Erdos-Renyi model G(n,p), fix a vertex i. Its degree d_i is the sum of the n - 1 independent Bernoulli(p) indicators for the potential edges incident to i, and its mean is d = (n - 1)p. Applying the cited small-deviation Chernoff inequality at relative deviation 0.1 gives P(|d_i - d| >= 0.1d) <= 2 exp(-c d) for some positive absolute constant c. This is a one-vertex concentration statement. It occurs inside Proposition 2.4.1 under the inherited dense-regime assumption d >= C log n, although that assumption is not used by this local calculation.
